title: Keyboard shortcut rendering in settings doesn't take keyboard layout into account
summary: Settings displays the digit-row shortcut as Ctrl+1 rather than Ctrl+& under French AZERTY.

judgment.rationale: The report has a concrete scenario, but the affected boundary is unverified.
evidence: On PowerToys 0.99.1 the reporter expects the unshifted French AZERTY key label Ctrl+& for the ZoomIt shortcut but sees Ctrl+1.
The report includes comparison screenshots and scripts; no comments, assignee or linked fix appear in the collected thread.
Inspected src/settings-ui/Settings.UI.Library/HotkeySettings.cs and Utilities/Helper.cs, which use LayoutMap for key names.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce the reported scenario on a current build and isolate the failing boundary before choosing a correction.

fix_assessment.rationale: A targeted correction may be applicable after the reported behavior and boundary are confirmed.

proposed_fixes.title: Investigate layout-aware Settings shortcut labels
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The layout or naming path used for rendering may not match the active layout for this shortcut; an incorrect mapping or stale UI is not established.
plan: Reproduce the ZoomIt shortcut under French AZERTY and US layouts and compare actual virtual-key semantics with its displayed name.
Trace the active thread layout and shortcut label refresh when switching layouts.
Correct only the demonstrated display mapping or refresh boundary without silently changing the stored shortcut or activation semantics.
Add focused tests for French and US layouts, layout switches and special non-printable keys.
verification: Shortcut labels match the effective active key meaning and refresh after layout changes.
Existing shortcuts continue to activate with the same stored virtual keys.

confidence.rationale: The scenario and relevant source path are known, but current behavior and the failing boundary are unverified.

issue_context.summary: Settings displays the digit-row shortcut as Ctrl+1 rather than Ctrl+& under French AZERTY.

The report includes comparison screenshots and scripts; no comments, assignee or linked fix appear in the collected thread.
inferences: The layout or naming path used for rendering may not match the active layout for this shortcut; an incorrect mapping or stale UI is not established.
initial_investigation: Inspected src/settings-ui/Settings.UI.Library/HotkeySettings.cs and Utilities/Helper.cs, which use LayoutMap for key names.

Inspected src/common/interop/keyboard_layout.cpp: the map uses the current thread keyboard layout and ToUnicodeEx and is refreshed by layout identity; the UI binding path and actual result were not reproduced.
Searched open upstream PRs for keyboard-layout shortcut work; no covering PR was established.

reproduce.title: Investigate layout-aware Settings shortcut labels
reproduce.version_requirement: Use the current PowerToys release and compare with 0.99.1 where practical.
prerequisites: Use a Windows test machine and preserve the original configuration.
setup: Enable French AZERTY and US keyboard layouts on a test Windows system; enable ZoomIt.
steps: 1. Select French AZERTY and inspect the Zoom toggle shortcut label and stored virtual key in Settings.
2. Compare the label with the actual key used to activate the shortcut.
3. Switch to US layout, reopen or revisit Settings, and compare the label and activation; switch back to French.
4. In a maintainer diagnostic session, inspect the layout supplied to key-name mapping and the UI update path.
reproduce.expected_result: The displayed label accurately describes the active shortcut under each layout without changing its activation semantics.
